speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy with feeding difficulties and abdominal distension; can you tell me if you are passing stool and urine normally?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Has there been any vomiting, and if so, is it forceful or green? Also, when was his last bowel movement, and has it ever been ribbon-like?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung's Disease (Congenital Aganglionic Megacolon). REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal Ultrasound for transition zone visualization. The combination of failure to pass meconium, ribbon-like stools, abdominal distension, and bilious vomiting in an infant is classic for this condition.
